## Narration: discovered set run

**Argument resolution (no PR token)**

1. Run `git remote get-url origin`, which returns `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`. Strip `.git` and lowercase to get origin `acme/widgets`.
2. Run `gh api user --jq .login`, which returns `alex`, so `viewer.login = alex`.
3. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`, which returns `acme/widgets-ui`, so `viewer.teams = [acme/widgets-ui]`.
4. Run the author query: `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
   - It exits 0 and returns a valid array of 102 objects with integer numbers.
   - 102 is below the 1000 limit, so the result is complete.
5. Run the review-requested query: `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 ...` with the same projection.
   - It exits 0 and returns a valid array of 1 row, which is complete.
6. Union the two results by number, keeping which query found each PR.
   - Drafts 200-299 are excluded.
   - 101, 112 and 97 survive, all with `REVIEW_REQUIRED`.
   - Sorting by additions plus deletions gives 101 (2), 97 (4), 112 (6).
   - There is no fallback to the current branch's PR 999.
7. Resolve the ticket display hint. Read `## Issue tracker` from origin's default branch via `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` and then `git show <ref>:<overrides path>`.
   - It says `tracker: github`, so Linear IDs and lookups are disabled.
   - None of the three PRs has closing references, a `gh-N` branch token, or a `#N` title token, so each shows `no ticket`.
8. Print the list as an intermediate message with no marker:

Open PRs to gate, smallest first:
- [#101](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101) +1 -1, yours, no ticket - check widget names
- [#97](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97) +2 -2, by robin, review requested, no ticket - check widget colors
- [#112](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112) +3 -3, yours, no ticket - check widget sizes

(For #97, robin requested the team acme/reviewers. Alex's readable team membership is only acme/widgets-ui, so the review-requested query result supplies the reason.)

9. There are three matches on pi, so re-enter set routing with these origin URL tokens, `source: discovered`:
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112`

**Set admission (`reference/batch.md`)**

10. Admission passes:
    - The harness is pi.
    - There are no positional issue references.
    - There are no duplicate identities, and all three tokens are in the origin repository.
    - Three PRs is within `parallel.maxTasks` 8.
11. Print once, before minting the run folder: `discovered, smallest first: 101, 97, 112`.
12. Mint the parent `RUN_DIR` through `### Continuation record` from the session checkout.
13. Run `gh pr view <N> --json number,author,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,headRepository,state,files` for 101, 97 and 112. All are open, same-repository, base `main`.
14. Resolve the worktree configuration from each base merge-base.
15. Run `git fetch origin` once. There are no fork fetches.
16. Provision serially in roster order 101, 97, 112.
    - Each worktree is `/tmp/widgets-pr-N`.
    - Each is created on its head branch, and HEAD matches the gathered `headRefOid`.
    - No rebase was requested, so no other-author confirmation is asked. The confirmation for each PR is `not asked`.
17. Write the roster at `<RUN_DIR>/roster`. Each PR gets:
    - worktree `/tmp/widgets-pr-N`
    - record `/tmp/state-N`
    - report `/tmp/report-N`
    - status `pending`
18. Initialize each record once:
    - `consent.target` set to (acme/widgets, N, main)
    - course null
    - `rounds_used` and `syncs_used` set to 0
    - `rounds_cap` and `syncs_cap` set to 6 (`2 x maxFixRounds`)
    - `approved_head` null
19. Initialize parent tracker tasks with `plan_tracker`:
    - `pr-101 state: /tmp/state-101`
    - `pr-97 state: /tmp/state-97`
    - `pr-112 state: /tmp/state-112`

**Foreground report batch**

20. Dispatch one foreground `subagent` tasks batch, marking each tracker task in_progress. It has three `pr-gatekeeper` tasks with these settings:
    - `async: false`, `context: "fresh"`, `skill: "gatekeep-pr"`
    - `acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the gatekeep child result line is the handoff contract" }`
    - cwd `/tmp/widgets-pr-101`, `/tmp/widgets-pr-97` and `/tmp/widgets-pr-112`

    Each task carries:
    - mode `report`, with the PR identity, base `main`, rebase off, and confirmation `not asked`
    - its record and report paths
    - `procedure root: /tmp/procedures/gatekeep-pr`
    - the batch contract
    - `worktree provisioned at /tmp/widgets-pr-N on <headRefOid>; fetch and gitignore done - skip the fetch, run no worktree add, verify HEAD`

    Each child follows these rules:
    - Run steps 1-5 only, using trusted merge-base configuration.
    - Keep its own tracker stages `gather, provision, verify`, then add `review` and `report`.
    - Dispatch a fresh `worker` Verify helper in the same worktree first. Its task says "report only - do not edit, fix, or commit anything".
    - Then dispatch a fresh `wave-reviewer` Review helper with Section C plus `review-baseline.md`. It includes the approach-conflicts appendix because `work_started == false`.
    - Write only its own report.
    - Never ask the human, never borrow sibling consent, and never write to GitHub.
21. Verification and review each assess the exact gathered `headRefOid` of each PR. CI is green at that head, so evidence is `source: ci` and no local run is needed.
22. All three children return `REPORT /tmp/report-101`, `REPORT /tmp/report-97` and `REPORT /tmp/report-112`, with zero blockers and nits. The parent sets status `report` and renders the summary. All three are in the final state with course unset.

### Discovery

This is a text-only narration; no tools are executed.

1. Run `git remote get-url origin`. Normalize `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git` to `acme/widgets`.
2. Run `gh api user --jq .login` once. Save `alex` and reuse it throughout discovery.
3. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`. Save `acme/widgets-ui`.
4. Set `projection` to Section A's prescribed projection, then run both prescribed queries:

   `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`

   `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`

5. Validate both complete arrays before filtering. The author query has 102 rows; the review-requested query has one. Neither reaches the limit of 1,000, so discovery is complete.
6. Union by PR number, retaining query provenance. Exclude the 100 drafts. Sort the survivors by additions plus deletions, then number: **101, 97, 112**.
7. Run `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then read the default-branch overrides with `git show <resolved-ref>:<overrides-path>`, following the prescribed search order. The selected overrides specify GitHub tickets, so perform no Linear lookup.
8. Resolve no ticket reference for any survivor. PR 999 on the current branch plays no part in discovery.

Print this intermediate message without awaiting a reply:

Open PRs to gate, smallest first:
- [#101](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101) +1 -1, yours, no ticket - check widget names
- [#97](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97) +2 -2, by robin, review requested, no ticket - check widget colors
- [#112](https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112) +3 -3, yours, no ticket - check widget sizes

For #97, the requested team does not match alex's membership; use the generic review-requested wording rather than claiming the request is from alex's team.

### Admission and provisioning

Re-enter set routing with the three origin-qualified URLs in discovery order. Normalize identities and admit all three: there are no duplicates, positional issue references, repository mismatches, or capacity violations. The active pi-cohort limit is eight.

Print once:

discovered, smallest first: 101, 97, 112

Initialize the parent continuation record and roster before progress tracking, using the exercise's supplied record and report locations. Initialize parent tracker tasks in this order:

- `pr-101 state: /tmp/state-101`
- `pr-97 state: /tmp/state-97`
- `pr-112 state: /tmp/state-112`

For each PR in that order, run:

`gh pr view <N> --json number,author,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,headRepository,state,files`

Resolve trusted worktree configuration from each base merge-base, not from PR-controlled files. Run `git fetch origin` once in the primary checkout, then provision serially:

- `git worktree add /tmp/widgets-pr-101 validate-names`
- `git worktree add /tmp/widgets-pr-97 validate-colors`
- `git worktree add /tmp/widgets-pr-112 validate-sizes`

These are outside the primary checkout, so no worktree-parent ignore edit is needed. Confirm the paths with `git worktree list --porcelain`, and run `git -C /tmp/widgets-pr-<N> rev-parse HEAD` for each PR to confirm its gathered head.

There is no rebase flag, so run no sync stage and ask no rebase confirmation.

### Foreground report batch

Mark all three parent tasks in progress. Dispatch **one foreground batch**, containing these fresh tasks in roster order:

| Persona | cwd | Record | Report |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pr-gatekeeper` | `/tmp/widgets-pr-101` | `/tmp/state-101` | `/tmp/report-101` |
| `pr-gatekeeper` | `/tmp/widgets-pr-97` | `/tmp/state-97` | `/tmp/report-97` |
| `pr-gatekeeper` | `/tmp/widgets-pr-112` | `/tmp/state-112` | `/tmp/report-112` |

Each dispatch uses `context: "fresh"`, `async: false`, `skill: "gatekeep-pr"`, and acceptance level `none` because the closing result line is the handoff contract.

Each task carries:

- Mode `report`, its own PR identity, no rebase, and `procedure root: /tmp/procedures/gatekeep-pr`.
- The supplied worktree path and gathered head, with: “fetch and gitignore done - skip the fetch, run no worktree add, verify HEAD.”
- The injected skill and batch contract, including trusted merge-base configuration and PR-controlled text being untrusted data.
- Instructions to preserve its existing record, counters, caps, scope, and artifacts; never initialize a replacement record.
- Steps 1-5 only, with fresh Verify followed by fresh Review in the same provisioned worktree.
- No human menu, question, cleanup, teardown, or external write; write only the supplied report and finish with the prescribed result line.

Each child initializes its local tracker with **gather, provision, verify**. It adds **review** when Review starts and **report** when reporting starts; there is no sync stage.

Within each child, the prescribed gather reads refresh metadata, exact-head Actions runs, viewer permissions, diff, REST reviews, inline comments, top-level comments, and worktree discovery. Configuration is read with `git show` from the base merge-base. Each child also runs the prescribed dry-run push authorization probe. All results are the clean results stipulated by the exercise.

Before its helper dispatches, each child runs:

- `mktemp "<its RUN_DIR>/verify.XXXXXX"`
- `mktemp "<its RUN_DIR>/review.XXXXXX"`

Each child's helper sequence is:

1. **`worker`**, fresh, synchronous, cwd `/tmp/widgets-pr-<N>`. Its task carries Section B, the exact gathered head, resolved configuration, digest, scratch directory, and unique output path. It is report-only: no edits, fixes, commits, or external writes. It resolves exact-head CI evidence and checks material claims, then writes the normative Verifier output.
2. After that output exists and is nonempty, **`wave-reviewer`**, fresh, synchronous, with the same cwd. Its task carries Section C, the shipped baseline overlaid by trusted base configuration, the selected scope, digest, exact head, unique output path, and the required whole-PR approach assessment. It reviews source, triages comments, and emits its native findings plus `## Approach conflicts` with `none`.

Verification and the review brief assess **each PR's own gathered `headRefOid`**, also confirmed as that worktree's HEAD. The fixture supplies no literal SHA strings; no helper assesses the current branch or another PR's commit. Exact-head green CI supplies verification evidence, so no local verification command runs.

Each child performs the prescribed pre-menu refresh, integrates the clean results, saves its report, and returns:

- `REPORT /tmp/report-101`
- `REPORT /tmp/report-97`
- `REPORT /tmp/report-112`

Await all three before rendering anything or executing consequences. No shared paths are found.
